word:hebrew:H1047.explanation: Beth-peor is a Hebrew proper name for a place. It functions as a geographical name rather than a general term describing an action, quality, or person. In English Bible renderings, it appears as “Bethpeor” or “Beth,” preserving the place-name character. The name occurs eight times in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Deuteronomy and Joshua, with references ranging from Deuteronomy 3:29 to Joshua 13:20. Its precise significance in any particular passage depends on the surrounding verse and context.

word:hebrew:H1102.explanation: Balam means to muzzle or to be held in.

word:hebrew:H1281.explanation: Bârîyach refers to a fugitive or something fleeing. It can describe a serpent as crooked or piercing. It can also refer to nobles.

word:hebrew:H1339.explanation: Bath-Sheba is the personal name of Solomon’s mother.

word:hebrew:H1375.explanation: This word means “cup,” referring to a vessel used to hold or serve liquid. It names a physical object in several Old Testament settings, including the account involving Joseph’s brothers and descriptions in Exodus. It may refer to one cup or to multiple cups. The word occurs 14 times in the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, with appearances in Genesis, Exodus, and Jeremiah. Its ordinary sense remains a tangible cup or container rather than an abstract idea.

word:hebrew:H1450.explanation: Gederoth is the name of a place in Palestine.

word:hebrew:H1506.explanation: Gezer means a piece or portion cut off from a whole.

word:hebrew:H152.explanation: Adrammelech is a proper name, rendered “Adrammelech,” rather than an ordinary word describing an action, quality, or object. It occurs three times in the Hebrew Old Testament, in two books. The name is connected with worship or bowing in the SEE records for 2 Kings 19:37 and Isaiah 37:38, so its normal scriptural use identifies a named figure associated with such worship. The exact role in each passage depends on the surrounding verse context.

word:hebrew:H1634.explanation: Gerem means bone. It can also refer to strength or the top.

word:hebrew:H1641.explanation: Gârar means to drag off roughly. It can also describe chewing the cud. It can also describe sawing stone.

word:hebrew:H1678.explanation: This word means “bear,” referring to the large wild animal. It functions as a noun, naming an animal rather than describing an action or quality. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs once, in Daniel 7:5. The word’s basic meaning is therefore straightforward: it identifies a bear. The precise force of the animal’s appearance in that passage belongs to the surrounding vision and verse context, but the word itself names the creature.

word:hebrew:H1717.explanation: Dad means breast. It can also refer to a teat.

word:hebrew:H1915.explanation: Hadak means to crush with the foot—to tread down.

word:hebrew:H1959.explanation: Heidad means an acclamation or shout.

word:hebrew:H2019.explanation: Hăphakpak means very perverse or froward.

word:hebrew:H2055.explanation: Vajezatha is a Hebrew personal name, functioning as the designation of an individual rather than as a general word describing an action, quality, or object. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Esther 9:9. Because this name appears only in that single occurrence and no further lexical definition is provided, its significance is carried by the person it identifies in that passage rather than by a broader recurring word sense.

word:hebrew:H215.explanation: Owr means to make luminous—to give light or make something shine.

word:hebrew:H2370.explanation: Chaza means to see or gaze upon. It can also describe dreaming.

word:hebrew:H2503.explanation: Helez is a personal name, referring to an individual rather than expressing an action, quality, or general idea. In the Hebrew Bible, it appears five times across four verses, consistently rendered “Helez.” Its occurrences are connected with genealogical records and references to the person in Israel’s history. Because it functions as a name, its meaning is primarily identification: it distinguishes Helez from other people named in the surrounding records.

word:hebrew:H259.explanation: Echad means one, referring to a single item. It can also mean first, marking the beginning of an order.

word:hebrew:H2662.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to the “Hepherites,” a group identified by its connection with Hepher. It functions as a plural name for those people rather than as a general description of an action, quality, or object. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it appears once, in Numbers 26:32, so its use is limited to this clan designation. The precise significance of the group in that verse depends on the surrounding passage and its account of Israel’s families.

word:hebrew:H2680.explanation: This Hebrew word means “half.” It identifies a divided portion rather than an action, quality, or person. In the Hebrew Bible corpus represented here, it occurs twice, both within one verse in 1 Chronicles. Its precise role in that genealogical wording depends on the surrounding verse, which is not included here; however, its ordinary lexical sense remains a division into two corresponding parts. word:hebrew:H2767.explanation: Chormah means a place in Palestine.

word:hebrew:H2789.explanation: Cheres means a piece of pottery. It can refer to an earthen vessel or a potsherd used for scraping.

word:hebrew:H2842.explanation: Chashash means dry grass or chaff.

word:hebrew:H2925.explanation: This Hebrew word means “captivity,” naming the condition of being held or carried away rather than remaining free. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at Isaiah 22:17. Because the available wording gives only this single established meaning and the verse text is not included here, the safest understanding is the basic noun: captivity itself. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but the word’s ordinary reference is clear.

word:hebrew:H2969.explanation: Ya'ah means to be suitable or fitting.

word:hebrew:H2987.explanation: Yebal means to bring. It can also mean to carry.

word:hebrew:H3001.explanation: Yabesh means to dry up, as when waters dry up. It can also describe grass withering.

word:hebrew:H3038.explanation: Jeduthun is the name of an Israelite.

word:hebrew:H3210.explanation: Jalon is the name of an Israelite.

word:hebrew:H3373.explanation: Yare means fearing or being afraid. It can also describe reverence toward God.

word:hebrew:H3405.explanation: Jericho is the name of a place in Palestine.

word:hebrew:H3540.explanation: Kedorlaomer is the name of an early Persian king, identified in Scripture as king of Elam.

word:hebrew:H3632.explanation: Kalil means complete or whole. It can also describe something done fully. As a noun, it can refer to a whole burnt offering.

word:hebrew:H3791.explanation: Kathab means something written, such as a writing or record. It can also refer to a register connected with genealogy.

word:hebrew:H3830.explanation: Lebush means a garment or clothing worn by a person.

word:hebrew:H3913.explanation: Latush means to sharpen by working an edge, including farming tools such as a plowshare, mattock, axe, or sickle.

word:hebrew:H398.explanation: Akal means to eat. It can also describe dining at a meal.

word:hebrew:H4040.explanation: This Hebrew word means a “roll,” naming a physical written item. It functions as a noun, identifying an object rather than describing an action, quality, or person. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs once, at Ezra 6:2. Since the surrounding verse text is not included here, its particular significance in that passage cannot be expanded beyond its basic sense: a roll.

word:hebrew:H4149.explanation: “Mosera” is a Hebrew place name, referring to a location rather than expressing an action, quality, or doctrine. It occurs three times in the Old Testament corpus, in Israel’s wilderness-travel records: twice in Numbers and once in Deuteronomy. The English rendering identifies it as “Mosera”; the precise significance of the place in any passage depends on the surrounding verse and journey account.

word:hebrew:H4291.explanation: Metaw means to arrive or reach, including extending as far as a point. It can also describe something happening or coming upon someone.

word:hebrew:H4332.explanation: Mishael is a personal name used for Israelites.

word:hebrew:H4457.explanation: Melqach means tweezers. Scripture renders it as tongs or snuffers.

word:hebrew:H4501.explanation: This Hebrew noun means “candlestick,” referring to a lampstand used among Israel’s sacred furnishings. It is especially associated with the tabernacle and temple, where it appears alongside other appointed objects and in instructions concerning its placement and use. The word occurs 42 times in the Hebrew Old Testament, with many occurrences in Exodus and several in Numbers, Chronicles, and Zechariah. Its repeated connection with commanded worship shows that it names a specific furnishing rather than a general source of light.

word:hebrew:H4538.explanation: Mesek means a mixture, specifically wine mixed with spices.

word:hebrew:H4574.explanation: Maadan means a delicacy or delight; it can also describe acting cheerfully.

word:hebrew:H4673.explanation: Matstsab means a fixed spot. It can also refer to a military post or garrison.

word:hebrew:H4710.explanation: Mitspun means a secret or hidden thing, such as a hidden treasure.

word:hebrew:H484.explanation: Almug refers to almug wood or trees, probably sandalwood.

word:hebrew:H4866.explanation: Mishber means the opening of the womb, the place from which a child comes forth.

word:hebrew:H4912.explanation: Mashal means a proverb or pithy saying. It can also describe a parable.

word:hebrew:H5007.explanation: Ne’atsah means scorn. It can also refer to blasphemy.

word:hebrew:H5133.explanation: Notsah means a pinion or wing feather and can also refer collectively to plumage.

word:hebrew:H5186.explanation: Natah means to stretch or spread out. It can also describe turning or bending away, including a moral deflection.

word:hebrew:H5335.explanation: Neziah is a Hebrew name preserved as “Neziah” in English Bible renderings. It refers to a person rather than expressing an action, quality, or object. This word occurs twice in the Hebrew Old Testament, once in Ezra 2:54 and once in Nehemiah 7:56. Since no explicit definition is given, its ordinary meaning is best treated as the personal name Neziah, not expanded beyond that.

word:hebrew:H5379.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to a "gift," something given to another person. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, in 2 Samuel 19:42. Its basic meaning is therefore focused and specific rather than broad or frequently repeated across different passages. The exact force of the word in that verse depends on the surrounding sentence and passage, but its ordinary lexical sense is a gift presented or given.

word:hebrew:H5397.explanation: Neshamah means breath, including the breath of life. It can also refer to spirit.

word:hebrew:H5429.explanation: Seah means a measure used for grain.

word:hebrew:H5465.explanation: Sad means the stocks, a restraint in which the feet are placed.

word:hebrew:H5560.explanation: Soleth means fine flour or meal. It is used for cakes and for offerings brought to Yahweh.

word:hebrew:H5582.explanation: Saad means to support, including strengthening, refreshing, or comforting someone.

word:hebrew:H5616.explanation: “Sepharvites” is a proper name identifying a people or group mentioned in the Hebrew Old Testament. It is not presented as a general description or action, but as the designation of a particular population. This word occurs once in the Hebrew corpus, in 2 Kings 17:31. Its precise significance in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but the word itself functions as the name “Sepharvites.”

word:hebrew:H5708.explanation: ʻêd means periodic menstrual flux. In the plural, it can also refer by implication to something soiled or filthy.

word:hebrew:H5731.explanation: Eden names the region associated with Adam’s home. It is also used as a personal name.

word:hebrew:H5843.explanation: This Hebrew noun means “counsel,” referring to advice or guidance offered to help determine a course of action. It describes considered direction rather than an action itself. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs once, in Daniel 2:14. The surrounding verse context is needed to understand the particular force of the word there, but its basic sense points to counsel given for a practical decision or response.

word:hebrew:H5911.explanation: Akor is the name of a place, rendered Achor in English.

word:hebrew:H5928.explanation: Alah means a holocaust, or burnt offering.

word:hebrew:H5964.explanation: Alemeth is a Hebrew proper name, rendered “Alemeth” in English. It identifies a person or name within genealogical records rather than expressing an ordinary action, quality, or object. The name occurs four times in the Hebrew Old Testament, all in 1 Chronicles. Its recorded uses are connected with family lines and birth or begetting relationships, so its significance comes primarily from identifying someone in those genealogies. The surrounding verse text would be needed to explain the specific person named in each occurrence.

word:hebrew:H6059.explanation: Anaq means to adorn with a necklace or chain. It can also mean to furnish someone liberally with supplies.

word:hebrew:H6198.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to the “Eranites,” a named group of people. It functions as a group designation rather than a description of an action, quality, or object. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at Numbers 26:36. With no verse text or wider context available here, its clearest ordinary sense is simply the name identifying this people group in that passage.

word:hebrew:H6226.explanation: This Hebrew word means “smoking,” describing something that is giving off smoke. It is a descriptive word rather than a name or action by itself, so its meaning points to a condition involving smoke. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs twice, once in Exodus 20:18 and once in Isaiah 7:4. The surrounding verse determines what is smoking in each passage.

word:hebrew:H6293.explanation: Paga means to meet or reach. It can also describe falling upon someone. It may also describe entreating for another person.

word:hebrew:H6352.explanation: Pecham means a coal, whether charred or live. Scripture also shows these coals being worked by a smith.

word:hebrew:H6420.explanation: This Hebrew word is rendered as “Palal,” and here it functions as a person’s name rather than as an ordinary action or description. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at Nehemiah 3:25. Because no explicit definition is provided and the surrounding verse text is not included here, its personal-name function is the clearest supported understanding. Its precise role in that verse depends on the surrounding context.

word:hebrew:H6514.explanation: This Hebrew word is a personal name, rendered as “Peruda” or “Perida.” It appears twice in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Ezra 2:55 and Nehemiah 7:57. The two spellings represent the same named individual or family designation in these parallel restoration-era lists. Because no ordinary descriptive gloss is supplied, the word should be understood primarily as a proper name rather than as a term describing an action, quality, or object.

word:hebrew:H6558.explanation: “Pharzites” is a name identifying a people group in the Hebrew Old Testament. It functions as a group designation rather than as a general description of an action, quality, or object. This word occurs once in the Hebrew Bible, at Numbers 26:20, so its precise historical identity is not established by the word alone. The name’s meaning is therefore best stated narrowly: it refers to the Pharzites, a distinct people named in that passage.

word:hebrew:H6561.explanation: Pâraq means to break off. Figuratively, it can mean to deliver or redeem.

word:hebrew:H6763.explanation: Tsela means a rib or a side. It describes a rib in the man's body and a side of the ark.

word:hebrew:H6802.explanation: Tsenephah means a ball. In its recorded use, something is tossed like a ball.

word:hebrew:H6947.explanation: Kadesh-Barnea is a place in the desert.

word:hebrew:H7012.explanation: Qimah means an arising, or rising up.

word:hebrew:H714.explanation: Ard is a Hebrew personal name, rendered “Ard” in English. It identifies a person mentioned in the Old Testament and appears twice in the Hebrew Bible, in Genesis 46:21 and Numbers 26:40. Because the available wording does not provide a broader definition, the safest meaning is the name itself rather than an abstract quality or action. Its precise role in either passage depends on the surrounding verse and genealogical context.

word:hebrew:H7166.explanation: Qarsol means an ankle, the joint or raised part of the foot.

word:hebrew:H7377.explanation: Riy means watering—irrigation or a shower.

word:hebrew:H7399.explanation: Rekush means property or goods, including possessions that have been gathered. It can describe goods belonging to a person or property belonging to a king.

word:hebrew:H7430.explanation: Ramas means to creep or move with short steps. Scripture applies it to living things moving on the earth and to creeping things there.

word:hebrew:H7513.explanation: This Hebrew word means “rafts.” It names a concrete waterborne structure used for floating or transport, and its plural sense refers to more than one raft. The word occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at 2 Chronicles 2:16. Since the verse text is not included here, its precise role in that sentence cannot be explained further. Its basic meaning remains a group of rafts used in connection with travel or moving goods by water.

word:hebrew:H758.explanation: Aram is a personal name. It can also refer to Syria or the Syrians.

word:hebrew:H761.explanation: Aramite means an Aramaean, commonly rendered Syrian in English.

word:hebrew:H7636.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to “cauls,” a specific item mentioned once in the Hebrew Old Testament. Its only recorded occurrence is Isaiah 3:18, so Scripture provides no broader pattern of use for this word elsewhere in the Hebrew corpus. The English rendering identifies the item by name, while the available record does not provide a fuller definition or additional occurrences. Its exact significance in Isaiah 3:18 must therefore be understood from that verse’s surrounding context.

word:hebrew:H7683.explanation: Shagag means to stray or go astray. It can also describe sin committed unknowingly.

word:hebrew:H7724.explanation: Sheva is the name of an Israelite.

word:hebrew:H7751.explanation: Shuwt means to move back and forth. It can also describe going about or traveling through a place.

word:hebrew:H7768.explanation: Shava means to cry out for help, especially in trouble.

word:hebrew:H7805.explanation: Shazaph means to tan by the sun. It can also mean to see or look upon.

word:hebrew:H7849.explanation: Shatach means to expand, spread out, or stretch out.

word:hebrew:H7940.explanation: Sacar is a Hebrew personal name, rendered “Sacar.” It identifies an individual rather than expressing an action, quality, or idea. The name occurs twice in the Old Testament Hebrew corpus, both times in 1 Chronicles: once in 1 Chronicles 11:35 and again in 1 Chronicles 26:4. Without the surrounding verse text, the name itself gives the person’s designation but does not establish further meaning or significance. Its normal function is simply to identify Sacar in the biblical record.

word:hebrew:H8062.explanation: This Hebrew word means “Shemidaites,” a group name for people identified by that designation. It functions as a collective name rather than describing an action, quality, or object. The word occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Numbers 26:32, so its normal use is limited to this single recorded occurrence. Without the surrounding verse text, the safest explanation is simply that it identifies a particular people group called the Shemidaites.

word:hebrew:H8080.explanation: Shaman means to become fat or to make something fat.

word:hebrew:H8167.explanation: “Seirah” is a proper place name, referring to a location rather than describing an action, quality, or person. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs once, in Judges 3:26. Because the word functions as a name, its basic meaning is its identification of that particular place; the surrounding verse is needed to explain its role in that passage. This name is rendered “Seirah” in the cited English rendering.

word:hebrew:H8189.explanation: Shaaraim is a proper place name, referring to a location rather than describing an action, quality, or person. It appears three times in the Hebrew Old Testament, each time as the name “Shaaraim.” Because the available passages do not provide a direct definition of the name itself, its meaning as an ordinary word cannot be stated more specifically. Its precise significance in any particular verse depends on the surrounding passage and how that location functions there.

word:hebrew:H8303.explanation: Shirjon means a peak of Lebanon. Sirion is the name used for Hermon.

word:hebrew:H839.explanation: Ashur is a name for an Ashurite.

word:hebrew:H8453.explanation: Toshab means a resident alien, a foreigner who dwells among a people. In Scripture, this includes someone living with others as a temporary resident.

word:hebrew:H8570.explanation: Tenubah means produce. It can refer to fruit from a tree or increase from a field.

word:hebrew:H8655.explanation: Teraphim means a family idol or idols.

word:hebrew:H875.explanation: Be'er means a well. It can also mean a pit.

word:hebrew:H981.explanation: Bata means to speak rashly or unadvisedly, with words uttered without due care. It can describe words spoken in an oath. It can also describe speech like the piercing of a sword.
